Kithkin Go-Wide: Small folk, big numbers. A flood of Kithkin and tokens turns Kinbinding into a growing anthem, and Brigid, Clachan's Heart pays you for every creature that turned up this turn. Pick this if you want a board that gets wider and taller at the same time.
Merfolk Tap-Tempo: Your creatures pay for your spells and then get paid for it. Convoke taps the school to cast, which is exactly what Sygg, Wanderwine Wisdom and the tap-triggers were waiting for, while Adept Watershaper makes a fully tapped board indestructible. For players who like tempo decks that never really tap out.
Elementals - Big Spells: The deepest tribe in the cube, pointed straight at the opponent's face. Every Elemental that enters pings in for Champion of the Path, Ashling, Rekindled keeps the fire coming, and Twinflame Travelers doubles the triggers outright. Pick this if you want your late game to be damage rather than a board.
Goblin Aristocrats: A swarm of Boggarts worth more dead than alive. Boggart Cursecrafter and Grub, Storied Matriarch drain a little every time a Goblin dies, and blight counters let you finish off your own tokens on demand. Pick this if you like a deck where chump-blocking is a resource rather than a concession.
Elves - Graveyard Perfection: Elves that count the ones already buried. Morcant's Eyes and its fellow payoffs grow with every Elf in the yard, so self-mill becomes acceleration instead of a cost, and High Perfect Morcant turns that pile back into a board. For players who want a tribal deck with a second dimension.
Faeries - Flash Tempo: Almost nothing you do happens on your own turn. Flash bodies and counterspells hold the game open while Voracious Tome-Skimmer and Bitterbloom Bearer pay you for every spell cast during an opponent's turn. Pick this if you enjoy playing draw-go and somehow still building a board.
Blight / -1/-1 Counters: The set's signature mechanic sells you oversized creatures at a discount, then asks you to manage the debt. Shadow Urchin turns every -1/-1 counter into value and Lasting Tarfire spends them as removal. For players who like a deck where the drawback is the engine.
Lifegain & Persist Recursion: Small creatures that refuse to stay dead, and a life total that keeps climbing. Isilu, Carrier of Twilight hands persist to the rest of the team while Reaping Willow and Emptiness rebuy whatever dies anyway. Pick this if you want to win a long attrition war without ever casting an expensive card.
Giants: Enormous bodies bought cheap, paid for with -1/-1 counters you were glad to spend. Boldwyr Aggressor hands the tribe double strike and Hovel Hurler turns the leftover counters into reach. Pick this if you want to cast things far above the curve and start swinging immediately.
Vivid - Many Colours Matter: A deck where every extra colour on the battlefield makes your cards bigger. Bloom Tender and a pile of duals stretch you to four or five colours, and Prismatic Undercurrents and Aurora Awakener scale directly off that count. For players who enjoy a greedy mana base that actually pays out.
Ramp, Treasure & Big Mana: Mana first, questions later. Treasures, dorks and Vibrance put you turns ahead of schedule, Aurora Awakener cashes that in for a board, and Raiding Schemes gives your noncreature spells conspire so a wide board doubles them. Pick this if you like turns that visibly snowball.
Reanimator & Self-Mill Value: Mill yourself, then take it all back at once. Most of the recursion here is small and cheap, but Bloodline Bidding returns an entire creature type from the yard and Twilight Diviner keeps the pile stocked. For players who would rather play from the graveyard than from hand.
Changeling Type-Matters: Every creature is every creature. Changelings switch on behold costs and choose-a-type cards in any deck, so Gathering Stone and Chronicle of Victory always have a target and Collective Inferno only ever kills their half of the board. Pick this if you like decks built out of rules text.
Convoke Go-Wide: Your board is your mana. Tokens flood in, convoke turns them into spells you should not be able to cast yet, and Eirdu, Carrier of Dawn hands convoke to your creature spells as well. Pick this if you like curving out and then casting something enormous several turns early.
Treefolk / Toughness Matters: Creatures that block all day and then hit like trucks. Doran, Besieged by Time makes everything deal damage equal to its toughness, turning the cube's butt-heavy bodies into real threats, and Bark of Doran spreads the trick around. For players who like a defence that turns lethal without warning.
Copy & Token-Copy: Make one good thing, then make several more of it. Mirrormind Crown turns each turn's first batch of tokens into copies of your best creature, and Mirrorform duplicates anything else worth having twice. Pick this if you enjoy assembling a two-card engine that makes a 1/1 maker win the game.
Voltron - Auras & Equipment: One creature, fully kitted out, swinging alone. Lofty Dreams and Stalactite Dagger stack the stats while flash protection Auras double as combat tricks, so your threat survives the removal aimed at it. For players who enjoy the tension of putting everything on a single body.
Lands-Matter / Landfall: Green ramp where every land drop is progress. Sapling Nursery is the cube's one true landfall payoff, fetches and landcycling keep the triggers coming, and Prismatic Undercurrents scales off the duals you were already playing. Pick this if you want a grindy green deck built out of its mana base.
Play-from-Exile Impulse Value: Play off the top of your library instead of out of your hand. Exile-and-cast effects turn spare mana into extra cards, and Goliath Daydreamer recasts your used instants and sorceries free on every attack. For players who like grinding out extra cards while still attacking every single turn.
Draw-Denial Stax: A lock built out of one card. Mornsong Aria turns every draw step into a tutor and a three-life clock, and you break the symmetry with hand attack and graveyard denial. Pick this if you want the strangest, meanest deck in the cube and do not mind drawing fewer cards yourself.
